title: Adaptive versioning: dual-run adapter migration and opt-in behavior flags
creator: Nadia Park
description:
Problem: We need a low-friction migration path for consumers when we change streaming semantics and tool-call payload shapes across API versions. Previous approaches (hard cutovers, long grace periods) either forced client changes quickly or kept old behavior indefinitely. Goal: design an adaptive dual-run migration pattern plus a consumer-side adapter kit and opt-in behavior flags to allow progressive rollout with observable safety nets.

Proposed approach:
1) Dual-run mode: allow a subset of requests to be executed in 'v2' runtime while mirroring results from the 'v1' runtime for internal regression checks. Mirroring is read-only for clients until opt-in is confirmed.
2) Behavior flags: expose stable flags at the route level (server-side) and SDK-level client opt-in flags that toggle streaming delimiters, function-call invocation vs. tool-call streaming, and structured JSON-output enforcement. Flags default to v1 behavior; opt-ins switch to v2 semantics.
3) Consumer adapter kit: lightweight JS/Python adapters that translate v2 streaming fragments into v1-compatible chunks so customers can adopt server-side improvements without immediate client-side changes.
4) Migration playbook: step-by-step guidance for PM/SEs to run canaries, measure regressions, collect prompt-level mismatches, and run targeted rollbacks.
5) Back-compat test harness: expand the regression replayer to support side-by-side comparisons, token-level diffs, and statistical drift scoring.

Why this is different: rather than a binary deprecation, this enables progressive adoption with tooling that reduces customer burden and gives us objective guardrails for quality and latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-run capability implemented in the routing layer with a configurable sample rate
Behavior flags implemented for streaming delimiter, function-call vs tool-call semantics, and structured-output strictness
Adapter libraries published for JS and Python that translate v2 streaming/tool-call payloads to v1-compatible shapes
Regression harness can replay mirrored pairs and produce a per-prompt drift score; thresholds documented
Migration playbook and customer-facing migration guide published with example scripts and rollback steps
Metrics dashboards show canary health (latency, token cost, correctness regression) and automatic alerts when thresholds exceed limits
rollout_plan: Wave 0: internal QA (100% mirror, 0% client-facing). Wave 1: select beta customers opt-in via SDK flag (1-5% traffic) with full mirrors. Wave 2: expanded opt-in (10-20%) with adapters enabled. Wave 3: default server-side behavior switches but flags remain for explicit opt-out for 90 days. Each wave requires passing regression score (<= 0.8 drift) and latency delta (<+10ms p50) for 48h.
test_plan: Add dual-run scenarios to the nightly regression matrix; compare outputs token-by-token and at structured-output field level
Create synthetic workloads that exercise streaming boundaries, partial tool-call invocations, and large KV cached sessions
Load test canary targets to verify batching/latency trade-offs with mirror overhead
Run client adapter e2e tests across Node/Python SDKs to validate no-regression compatibility for representative apps
